title: Accessibility audit and fixes
when: The user asks to check or improve the accessibility of a page or app, or to meet WCAG.
prompt:
Goal: A prioritized list of WCAG problems found in the files and the fixes applied, so the core tasks work by keyboard and screen reader.
Steps:
1. Structure: lang on html, one h1, headings in order, landmarks (header, nav, main, footer), a skip link to main.
2. Names: every img has alt (empty for decoration), every control has a label, icon buttons have aria-label, links say where they go.
3. Keyboard: every action reachable with Tab, Enter and Space, no traps, visible :focus-visible styles, logical order.
4. Color: text contrast 4.5 to 1 (3 to 1 for large text and UI borders), and no meaning by color alone.
5. Dynamic content: status messages in aria-live regions, dialogs with role, name, focus moved in and returned.
6. Write findings as: issue, WCAG criterion, location, fix; fix the critical ones first.
Quality bar:
- Native elements are used before ARIA.
- Every finding points to a file and element.
- Fixes do not change the visual design more than needed.
Pitfalls:
- Adding role="button" to a div instead of using a button.
- aria-label that disagrees with visible text.
- Removing outlines without a replacement.
Verify:
- [ ] Images have alt and controls have labels.
- [ ] Focus styles exist.
- [ ] Links have real text.
- [ ] The page has lang and a main landmark.
Output: Fixed HTML and CSS, plus a findings list with severity and status.

examples.input: revise a acessibilidade do meu site
examples.output: 14 findings: 5 missing labels, icon buttons unnamed, no focus style; all critical fixed
